Posterior predictive checks of a Bayesian calibration model

Source: R/calibration_ppc.R
calibration_ppc.Rd

Compares the observed share of true positives among the reviewed clips with its posterior predictive distribution, overall and within groups: bins of score (a reliability check), sites, species and any column of the validation data given in group (e.g. the month of the recording). A calibration that fits on average can still miss within groups: a detector whose precision drifts with the season, for instance, shows up as months with observed shares outside their predictive intervals, and would bias the detection histories built from the model.

Usage

calibration_ppc(
  fit,
  validations = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  bin_width = 0.1,
  min_n = 15,
  prob = 0.9,
  flag = 0.05,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

fit

Model returned by fit_calibration() with engine = "brms".

validations

The calibration data the model was fitted to, in the same row order, with any columns named in group (keep them with read_validations(keep = )). NULL uses the data stored in fit, which only hold the columns of the formula.

group

Optional character vector of columns of validations to check within, besides score bins, sites and species.

bin_width

Width of the score bins. Bins with fewer than min_n clips are merged with their neighbour.

min_n

Smallest number of clips in a score bin.

prob

Probability of the predictive interval.

flag

Groups with a p-value below flag or above 1 - flag are flagged.

n_draws

Number of posterior draws; NULL uses all.

seed

Seed of the choice of draws and of the predictive simulation. The global random number generator is left as it was.

Value

A tibble with one row per check and group: check ("overall", "score", "site", "species" or a column of group), group, n (clips), observed (share of true positives), pred_mean, pred_lower and pred_upper (posterior predictive mean and interval of the share), p_value and flagged. Plot it with plot_calibration_ppc().

Details

For each group, the test statistic is the share of true positives, \(T(y) = \bar y\), and the Bayesian p-value is the mid-p \(\Pr(T(y^{rep}) > T(y)) + \Pr(T(y^{rep}) = T(y)) / 2\), so that ties, frequent in small groups of binary verdicts, count half on each side. Values close to 0 or 1 mean that the model under- or over-predicts the share of true positives in that group (Gelman et al. 2013, Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., ch. 6). The checks reuse the clips the model was fitted to, so they are lenient: a flagged group is a misfit worth modelling (e.g. a group effect in the calibration formula), whereas no flag is not proof of a good fit.

See also

calibration_diagnostics() for convergence, which should be checked first.
